definition: In machine learning, a neural scaling law is an empirical scaling law that describes how neural network performance changes as key factors are scaled up or down.
details: These factors typically include the number of parameters, training dataset size, and training cost. Some models also exhibit performance gains by scaling inference through increased test-time compute (TTC), extending neural scaling laws beyond training to the deployment phase.
story: Think of an orchestra warming up: no single instrument carries the piece, but together they make the sound. At the bottom of every machine is a design — the shape of it, and how its pieces talk to each other. The layout decides what the machine can even attempt, before it learns a single thing. The shape of the machine is half the idea. And that shape of the machine — Neural scaling law — is what makes everything else possible.
